title: Domain Service

validation.research: Evans's original accessible DDD Reference, Services on printed page 14, establishes significant domain operations without a natural entity or value-object owner, standalone contracts, and domain-language naming. The article explains the original Services label while qualifying the overloaded term. Vernon's publisher sample is explicitly cited as the chapter overview on printed page xxv, supporting focused stateless domain services and integration uses; no access to the full Services chapter is claimed. Microsoft's tactical DDD documentation distinguishes domain decisions from application orchestration and deployed microservices. Randy Stafford's Service Layer catalog defines application boundaries and coordination. Fowler's Anemic Domain Model warns against extracting behavior that belongs on domain objects. Official Python sources support frozen fields and min key/default behavior. The room policy, code, diagrams, and booking scenario are original teaching material.

Checks verify exact-seat eligibility, required-feature subsets, case-sensitive feature/ID semantics, smallest-capacity selection, deterministic room-ID ties, every permutation of the four demo offers, generator and list inputs, input preservation, empty/no-match outcomes, invalid request/candidate types, malformed counts and features, Boolean/fractional/zero/negative rejection, nonblank IDs, duplicate-ID rejection even for ineligible candidates, immutable snapshots, and large integer seat counts. Two calls can select A from the same snapshots, while refreshed offers excluding A select B, explicitly demonstrating that selection does not reserve a room. The model imports only dataclasses and performs no I/O.

example_limits: A pure module-level function compares a finite supplied set of immutable room-offer snapshots. The teaching policy minimizes suitable seat count, then uses exact case-sensitive room-ID ordering; it establishes deterministic choice, not fairness. Candidate offers are assumed to be a consistent, authorized view for the requested time. The example contains no calendar, availability query, booking state, authorization mechanism, persistence, transaction, concurrency protection, or external-effect delivery. It does not claim that all domain services are pure, that stateless dependencies are thread safe, or that cross-aggregate operations share an atomic commit. Normal API immutability is not protection against deliberate runtime bypass. An availability-query failure must remain distinguishable from no suitable supplied candidate. The second diagram describes a conceptual booking-conflict protocol, not an implemented reservation store.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
